jobs.title: Applied AI Architect - EDU
jobs.description:
About The Team

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

Within Education, we partner with universities, schools, research institutions, and countrywide education systems to advance responsible, mission-aligned uses of AI. These environments require more than technical deployment: success depends on institutional trust, thoughtful governance, stakeholder education, change management, and a value narrative that resonates with academic leaders, researchers, IT teams, faculty, administrators, and students.

About The Role

As an Applied AI Architect for Education, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of education customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will act as the “CTO of your book of business,” shaping each institution’s AI strategy and guiding its journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable institutional impact.

You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Edu, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate institutional priorities into a focused portfolio of use cases, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable value and growth. The Account Director owns the commercial strategy; you own the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value.

You will work across academic, research, administrative, and operational contexts—helping customers determine where AI can responsibly improve teaching and learning, accelerate research, strengthen student and faculty services, and make institutional operations more effective. You will account for the realities of education environments, including shared governance, complex stakeholder networks, academic calendars, accessibility, data privacy, responsible-AI expectations, and the need to build confidence among communities with differing levels of AI readiness.

You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, education programs, and partners. This role calls for strong education-sector fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy, academic and operational workflows, and hands-on technical conversations.

In This Role, You Will

Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of existing education customers and pre-sales prospects.
Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, value-realization path, and expansion opportunities.
Lead discovery with institutional executives, academic leaders, researchers, faculty, administrators, and technical teams to identify and prioritize use cases connected to meaningful institutional objectives.
Translate education priorities into clear Applied AI Architectures spanning models, applications, institutional data, identity, integrations, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, and deployment.
Guide institutions through technical evaluations, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, and proofs of value, building confidence in both the solution and its responsible path to production.
Translate institutional objectives into actionable adoption roadmaps with clear workstreams, sequencing, milestones, stakeholder ownership, governance, risks, success measures, and change-management needs.
Develop a focused use-case portfolio across areas such as teaching and learning, research, student and faculty services, knowledge management, software development, and administrative operations.
Translate institutional objectives into actionable adoption roadmaps with clear workstreams, sequencing, milestones, stakeholder ownership, governance, risks, success measures, and change-management needs.
Build trusted relationships and technical champions across CIOs, CTOs, CISOs, provosts, deans, research leaders, faculty, administrators, and other institutional stakeholders.
Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, Product, Research, education specialists, partners, and other delivery teams.
Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged.
Track adoption, usage, account health, production readiness, and measurable customer impact, intervening early when risks threaten value realization.
Identify repeatable education patterns and reusable architectures that can accelerate responsible adoption across institutions, departments, campuses, and education systems.
Translate field insights into actionable feedback for Product, Engineering, and Research, representing the needs and production patterns of education customers.
Help identify expansion opportunities where OpenAI can support additional academic, research, administrative, or operational workflows.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have significant experience in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, solutions engineering, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical customer success.
Have guided complex organizations from technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable value realization.
Build credibility with senior technical and business leaders while communicating equally well with hands-on engineers.
Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, data integration, identity, security, and privacy.
Understand modern AI systems, frontier LLM models, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, or enterprise AI workflows.
Can prototype, explain technical tradeoffs, and work confidently with APIs, SDKs, and languages such as Python or JavaScript.
Exercise sound judgment about when to go deep personally, when to involve specialists, and how to define clear handoffs and ownership.
Have experience developing technical account plans, prioritizing complex customer portfolios, and connecting adoption to measurable outcomes.
Can translate technical capabilities into institutional value across priorities such as student success, research productivity, faculty enablement, administrative effectiveness, accessibility, risk, and governance.
Communicate clearly and can turn ambiguity, competing stakeholder needs, and complex technical choices into a practical narrative, executive decision, or action plan.
Work collaboratively across disciplines and care deeply about helping education institutions deploy advanced AI safely, responsibly, and in service of their missions.
Meaningful experience with education technology, higher education, K–12 systems, research institutions, or similarly mission-driven and consensus-oriented environments is an added bonus

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

Location: San Francisco Bay Area, CA

Overview

The Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) will be the ultimate problem solver, an elite member of First Resonance's "Delta" FDSE, being deployed to our customers' sites to overcome their most demanding challenges. In this role, you will be working hand-in-hand with customers by getting deeply involved in their operations, understanding their unique problems, and developing tailor-made solutions that integrate seamlessly with ION.

Fired up to support eVTOLs, rockets, robots, and autonomous vehicles makers? As an FDSE, you will directly impact our customers’ ability to achieve these goals by interpreting their needs, developing software solutions from concept to delivery, and ensuring a high level of customer satisfaction. Your days could range from working with a customer's engineers to design a new feature that automates a laborious process to being the point person in debugging an issue blocking their production team.

Responsibilities & Duties

Serve as a deployed technical expert, providing hands-on assistance with the implementation, usage, and further development of ION.
Collaborate with customers to understand their most pressing problems to develop coherent strategies & intelligent solutions (build custom web apps, wrangle large-scale data, etc)

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Growth Partner, NAM
jobs.description:
About Hilbert

Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth. Fully agentic by design, Hilbert shrinks months-long decision cycles to minutes. From Fortune 10 enterprises to beloved brands like FreshDirect, Blank Street, and Levain Bakery, operators run their growth on Hilbert. We're backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z).

Forward Deployed Growth Engineers are a new, dedicated customer team at Hilbert, sitting in our Foundations Tribe. You'll work hand in hand with our Growth Science and Product teams, who own the product's logic, models and playbooks, and take that expertise into every customer, from the first meeting to the moment Hilbert is running their growth.

What the role is

This is customer success delivered with growth expertise. You'll join each of your accounts as soon as the lead comes in. You'll help shape the use cases during the sales cycle and keep owning the account through deployment and live usage. You own two commercial outcomes: proof-of-concept conversion

and existing account revenue growth

. We also measure time to first value, sustained product adoption and the share of routine customer needs you handle independently.

Two things make this role different from most customer success jobs. First, you're forward-deployed: you'll travel with our GTM team around 50% of the time, sit in the room with our customers' leadership, and become the person they call when they want to move faster. Second, you're a growth operator, not a ticket handler: our customers buy growth, and you'll help them own their use cases in Hilbert, from paid media, CRM and retention to discounts, merchandising and demand forecasting, and read the results back with them . You are expected to develop a deep understanding of Hilbert’s capabilities, communicate clearly and effectively with customers, and proactively manage customer relationships to maximize the value delivered to every customer.

You'll be part of the first cohort of this team, reporting to the Head of Forward Deployed Growth in our Foundations Tribe and working day to day with the GTM team and delivery engineering pod in your region. You'll learn our data sources, deployment methods and the problems our customers bring us alongside our Growth Science, Product and data teams, and you'll handle most routine customer needs independently. When an account needs deeper expertise, you'll bring in our subject-matter experts and turn what you learn into answers, case studies and examples the whole team reuses.

What you'll do

Own a portfolio of accounts end-to-end: get assigned as soon as a lead comes in, shape the use cases with GTM and sales engineering through close, and stay accountable for onboarding coordination, customer follow-ups and blocker tracking.
Convert pilots into long-term partnerships: define success criteria with the customer up front, keep the proof of concept on track, and make the business case for expansion with numbers you can defend.
Grow account revenue: find the next highest-impact use case inside each customer and turn it into new scope.
Be the customer's trusted growth advisor: lead demos and working sessions, help customers put agreed use cases into practice, train their teams, review results, and identify what is blocking adoption.
Drive real business transformation: go beyond usage and make sure the results change how the customer's business runs.
Get the customer's data in: scope the data each use case needs, agree with their data team how it reaches Hilbert, and run the timeline with our data engineers until it is usable. Do it again whenever a new use case needs new data.
Capture how each customer measures their business: their KPIs, definitions and business rules, set up in Hilbert so every answer matches their numbers.
Manage every stakeholder: from the C-level sponsor to the marketing, growth and data teams who use Hilbert every day, and keep them aligned as the account grows.
Build rapport in person: travel with our GTM team around 50% of the time, shadow and then lead customer sessions, and know the product better than anyone else in the room.
Cover most customer needs yourself, and know when to escalate: you are expected to handle around 80% of customer needs independently from the very first assignment, building toward the capability to cover 95% of everything a customer brings. For everything else, engage our Growth Science, Product, and Data teams efficiently by providing clear customer context, business impact, relevant evidence, and what you have already investigated. Respect their time by minimizing unnecessary meetings and prioritizing clear, asynchronous communication. Own the follow-up, keep the customer informed, and ensure key learnings feed into the product roadmap.
Expand across departments and use cases: map which other teams (paid media, CRM, merchandising, pricing, finance) can run their decisions on Hilbert, find the next highest-impact use case in each, and turn it into new scope.
Embed Hilbert into activation surfaces: connect Hilbert’s outputs to the tools where the customer’s teams already act, from ad platforms and CRM/CDP to promo, merchandising and planning systems, so every insight flows straight into execution and becomes part of the daily workflow.
Join GTM funnel reviews: take part in the regular funnel reviews with the GTM team, and know which leads are coming to you next.
Grow the shared library: add answers, case studies and customer examples, so expert guidance becomes something the whole team reuses.

What you bring

Around 5 to 8 years of experience: an engineering or natural sciences background, followed by an analytical role in management consulting or a similar setting; pure customer success leaders with a strong analytical edge are also welcome.
Strongly analytical: you write SQL and understand customer data sources, key business definitions, data coverage and freshness, and the meaning and limitations of model outputs well enough to explain them and investigate routine questions. You can build a business case and present it to a CFO or CMO.
Driven by real business transformation: insight isn't enough until it changes how the customer's business runs.
Continuous learning: you don't know insurance or grocery yet, and you'll figure it out fast. You're a problem solver who hacks most of the job yourself and knows exactly who to bring in for the rest.
Excellent with customers: polished and high-energy, at ease in every customer conversation from small talk to the boardroom, credible with senior stakeholders, and able to build relationships that outlast a single project.
Strong stakeholder management is a must: you navigate complex organizations and keep senior and day-to-day stakeholders aligned.
Happy to travel often across your region, around 50% of the time and sometimes to a different customer city every week, and to work with an owner's mindset in a fast-moving startup.
Nice to have: deep vertical expertise in retail, grocery, or financial services, or existing relationships with enterprise B2C companies.

Reporting and location

You report to the Head of Forward Deployed Growth and work closely with the Head of GTM, North America, as the growth counterpart to the region’s GTM team. You’re on the move with GTM, joining new leads and customer meetings from the first conversation. Our Growth Science and Product teams own the product’s logic, models and playbooks, train you on them and support you on the deepest problems, and the delivery engineering pod in North America builds and runs each deployment with you. You are based in our New York or San Francisco office, hybrid, with travel to customers across the region of around 50 percent.

Compensation

Base salary, plus variable pay tied to performance and the revenue you help drive (proof-of-concept conversion, renewals and expansion), plus equity. Details are shared in next steps.

Interview process

Recruiter screen, 30 minutes.
GTM interview with the Head of GTM, North America, 30 minutes: a customer relationship you owned, from first meeting to live usage or expansion, and how you managed the stakeholders along the way.
Hiring manager interview, 30 minutes: how you work with customers and with our Growth, Product and GTM teams.
Growth case with our Growth team, 60 minutes: a real customer case, from the business problem and the data it needs to the use case, the success criteria and the business case for expansion.
Team and final interviews: meet the people you’ll work with day to day, and our leadership.
References: two from clients, one from a colleague you worked with on customer accounts.

Why join us

At Hilbert, we move fast, work collaboratively, and give people real ownership over their impact. As a fast-growing company, there's no shortage of room to grow — you'll take on new challenges quickly and shape the path as you go.

On top of that, here’s how we take care of our team:

Health, handled. We cover 100% of your health, dental, and vision premiums, including fertility coverage like IVF and egg freezing, with the option to add your spouse or dependents at additional cost.
Future you will thank you. A 401k plan, with an employer match that vests from day one.
Work from anywhere. Two weeks a year to take your laptop somewhere new, whether that’s a beach in Mallorca or your family’s kitchen table.
Getting here, on us. A monthly commuter stipend for your trips to our San Francisco or New York office.
Lunch is on us. A daily lunch stipend on office days, so the only thing you have to decide is where to eat.
Sharpen your English. Business English classes, for when the boardroom pitch needs to land perfectly.
And many more. We’re always cooking up new ways to support our team. Come build the future with us, and grow alongside a company that’s investing in yours.

Hilbert is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive culture, and we welcome applicants of all backgrounds. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

Experience with agentic architectures, including multi-step reasoning, orchestration frameworks, tool and function calling, and agent evaluation.
Experience with AI data infrastructure such as vector stores, graph databases, Redis, DynamoDB, and ElastiCache.
Experience with data governance tools and practices, including Unity Catalog, data lineage, access controls, and audit trails.
Experience with Spark, distributed computing, and large-scale data processing.
Experience designing human-in-the-loop systems, guardrails, LLM output evaluation, and responsible AI practices.

When you go the distance for our clients, we go the distance for you. We’re looking for a hands-on Senior AI Engineer who loves to build and experiment. Some projects will be fast-turnaround proofs of concept, while others will evolve into scalable internal tools and platforms. You’ll work closely with cross-functional teams to bring AI-powered ideas into production and help shape best practices for applied AI across the organization.

When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

What You’ll Be Doing...

As a Principal Forward Deployed AI Engineer within Verizon’s Data Analytics team, you will embed directly into the frontline of Verizon’s core Business Units to solve our most critical, ambiguous, and high-stakes operational challenges. Operating with total technical ownership, you will architect, build, and deploy production-grade agentic systems, enterprise RAG engines, full-stack microservices, and decision systems into live operations.

You are a technical anchor: you pair deep systems craftsmanship with a product mindset, cutting through operational ambiguity to design production architectures, implement custom orchestration layers (via LangGraph, Temporal, or custom state machines), and enforce context management strategies that scale into enterprise assets. Beyond shipping point solutions, you will run workloads reliably on Domino, Airflow, and Kubernetes, abstracting bespoke code into reusable SDKs, shared libraries, and architectural playbooks that scale company-wide.

Key Responsibilities Include

End-to-End Architectural Blueprinting: Defining the full-stack architecture for embedded AI initiatives, including multi-agent orchestration, state machines, latency/cost budgets, security boundaries, and enterprise back-end integrations.
Agentic Orchestration Engineering, Workflow Automation and Governance: Architect stateful agent workflows complying with established agentic governance rules, using tools like LangGraph, Temporal, or event-driven state machines, establishing strict protocols for tool calling, execution sandboxing, and deterministic fallback logic.
Context & Retrieval Systems: Designing production RAG infrastructure incorporating hybrid search, re-ranking algorithms, metadata filtering, and semantic caching, directly informing and scaling Verizon’s context architecture.
Runtime & Cloud Deployment: Deploying production agent services and scheduled workflows to target runtimes (e.g., Domino Data Lab, Apache Airflow, Kubernetes microservices, and serverless compute across AWS, GCP, or Azure).
Evaluation Harness Design: Architecting offline and online evaluation frameworks (e.g., LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic test generation, human-in-the-loop review queues, live A/B rollouts) to measure model drift, context hallucination rates, and task completion metrics.
Platform Codification & IP Creation: Generalizing custom domain deployments into reusable internal SDKs, API primitives, and modular UI components; mentor engineers across the organization and draft technical documentation for Verizon patent disclosures.
Strategic Discovery & Scoping: Embed alongside BU leadership to map intricate operational processes, cut through organizational noise, and isolate the highest-leverage intervention points where applied AI delivers measurable uplift.
Executive Translation: Serving as the technical authority in the room with BU Vice Presidents and Managing Directors, demystifying algorithmic behaviors, failure modes, and performance trade-offs.

What We’re Looking For...

You’ll need to have:

Bachelor’s degree or four or more years of work experience.
Six or more years of relevant experience required, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training.
Extensive hands-on experience leveraging frontier LLMs (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini) and agentic developer frameworks (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to build scalable solutions and achieve core business milestones.
Experience with containerized deployments (Docker), API design, and cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
Advanced full-stack programming mastery in Python, SQL, and modern JavaScript/TypeScript stacks.
Demonstrated ability to independently scope ambiguous technical initiatives and present architectural designs to senior executive stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to interface directly with enterprise stakeholders, translate ambiguous business requirements into technical architectures, and lead project delivery end-to-end.

Even Better If You Have

Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related technical field.
Experience building and scaling centralized context platforms or enterprise search engines similar to Verizon's internal enterprise context layer platforms.
Proven track record implementing both offline evaluation benchmarks and online evaluation/observability pipelines (latency, token costs, hallucination tracking, eval-driven development).
Proven experience deploying containerized services and data workflows across enterprise platforms such as Domino Data Lab, Apache Airflow, Kubernetes (EKS/GKE), and hyperscaler cloud environments (AWS/GCP/Azure).
Proven track record designing offline/online eval harnesses, guardrail frameworks, and observability systems (latency, token optimization, tracing).
Prior forward-deployed engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting experience in top-tier technology firms or hyperscalers.
Record of turning one-off operational builds into enterprise-wide shared libraries, with associated technical publications or filed patents.
Domain knowledge in telecommunications, network capacity optimization, capital planning, or large-scale customer care operations.
Deep expertise in retrieval and context architectures: designing production RAG pipelines, vector databases (e.g., pgvector, Milvus, Pinecone), hybrid search (dense + sparse/lexical), and dynamic context management.

If Verizon and this role sound like a fit for you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every “even better” qualification listed above.

Where you’ll be working

In this hybrid role, you'll have a defined work location that includes working from home and a minimum of three days per week in the office, which will be set by your manager. Employees are responsible for maintaining compliance with hybrid work policies.

40

We also offer a matched 401(k) savings plan, up to 8 company paid holidays per year and up to 6 personal days per year, paid parental leave, adoption assistance and tuition assistance, plus other incentives, we’ve got you covered with our award-winning total rewards package. Job Description

Position Summary

We aspire to be the premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company. We're at the forefront of research to deliver innovative health solutions that advance the prevention and treatment of diseases in people and animals. The Cyber Applied AI team is looking for a Senior Data Scientist to build detection and investigation analytics over enterprise security data. The work is statistical: finding unusual behavior in very high-volume network and endpoint telemetry, measuring similarity between security events, correlating alerts from multiple sources into unified incidents mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, and turning threat intelligence into structured, usable data. The person in this role takes an analytical method from idea through validation and into production, and owns the data pipelines that feed it.

This is a senior individual contributor role for a data scientist who also engineers. The person in it designs the method, builds the pipelines and services that run it, deploys it on Azure or AWS, and keeps it in production. That includes applied AI work: building AI-driven analysis systems that use Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools over security data stores to automate investigation and shorten triage, and exposing results through APIs and automated reporting.

Responsibilities

Build and maintain statistical anomaly detection over network telemetry at the scale of billions of records per day, using behavioral baselines, percentile thresholds (p95/p99), new and rare entity detection, and feature engineering.
Design correlation frameworks that use IDF weighting, entity similarity metrics, and MITRE ATT&CK mappings to aggregate EDR and other security telemetry into unified security events.
Implement these methods as production workflows in Azure Data Explorer using KQL functions and materialized views.
Evaluate detection and correlation methods with defined metrics (precision, recall, false positive rate, time to triage), validate them against labeled incidents and analyst feedback, and monitor for drift once in production.
Build pipelines that extract CVEs, indicators of compromise, and other structured intelligence from unstructured sources such as security news and vendor reporting.
Design AI-driven security analysis systems that use MCP tools against Azure Data Explorer and threat intelligence services to automate investigations and reduce triage time.
Turn analytical methods into repeatable detection and investigation workflows with automated reporting.
Design and operate the data pipelines that feed the analytics, including batch and streaming ingestion on AWS (S3, Lambda, Glue, Step Functions, Kinesis) and Azure.
Write ETL/ELT transformations in Spark and Python for large cybersecurity datasets.
Identify where a purpose-built analytical system can replace a commercial product and build it when the economics justify it.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in data science, Statistics, Physics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.
At least 5 years building statistical or machine learning methods and engineering them into production systems, including the data pipelines, cloud services, and APIs around them.
Hands-on experience with statistical anomaly detection, behavioral baselining, or similarity-based correlation on datasets in the hundreds of millions of records or larger.
Experience with security telemetry (network, endpoint/EDR, cloud, or identity) and familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
Strong Python and SQL. Working experience with an analytics query language such as KQL and with Spark or PySpark.
At least 3 years building data pipelines on Azure or AWS, including both batch and streaming ingestion.
Able to explain a method and its limits to engineers, analysts, and managers.

Preferred

Master's degree in data science, Statistics, Physics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field and at least 5 years of experience
Production experience with Azure Data Explorer, KQL functions, and materialized views.
Experience extracting structured intelligence (CVEs, IOCs) from unstructured text.
Experience building AI-driven analysis systems with LLM applications, AI agents, or MCP tools (for example Microsoft Foundry) over security data.
Experience with AWS data lake tooling: S3, Glue, Lambda, Step Functions, Kinesis.
Computer vision or deep learning work with PyTorch.
A record of replacing a commercial tool with an in-house analytical solution and measuring the savings.
Experience in pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or another regulated industry.

Required Skills

Business Intelligence (BI), Database Design, Data Engineering, Data Modeling, Data Science, Data Visualization, Machine Learning (ML), Software Development, Stakeholder Relationship Management, Waterfall Model

Reassignment Applicants : Eligible Reassignment clients should contact their Disability Counselor for assistance.

This position has recently been accreted by UAW RP union and will be a part of that union moving forward.

This position has the option of working a hybrid (preferred) or remote schedule.

Description

UC San Diego Health is on a journey to build and mature enterprise applied artificial intelligence capabilities that deliver meaningful, measurable impact at scale across the health system. This work reflects a sustained organizational commitment to developing these capabilities as a core part of how care is delivered and supported. The purpose of UCSDH’s applied AI efforts is grounded in the quadruple aim, using AI-enabled technologies to simultaneously expand access to care, improve clinical and operational outcomes, enhance quality and safety, and support a better experience for both patients and care teams. A key focus is leveraging real-time data, predictive, generative, and hybrid models, and increasingly automated interventions to demonstrably achieve impact at scale across the health system.

Central to this strategy is the Mission Control vision, which brings together real-time data and applied AI–driven decision support to provide system-wide insight and action across the care continuum, including population health. This initiative serves both as a delivery layer for targeted point solutions across the health system and as a centralized hub for system-level assessment, prediction, and coordinated action. The supporting technology landscape is intentionally dynamic, with an emphasis on identifying best-fit solutions over time while scaling a cohesive enterprise platform that integrates complementary tools and capabilities.

This position operates within the Jacobs Center for Health Innovation and is integrated into UC San Diego Health Information Services, sharing leadership, data, and infrastructure, while driving translational innovation and supporting enterprise operations at scale.

Position And Team

UC San Diego Health is seeking a Senior Data Scientist to work within the Joan & Irwin Jacobs Center for Health Innovation (JCHI) on all phases of AI model design and development. The role is responsible for the full model lifecycle, including intake and review, data preparation, model development, evaluation, pre-deployment preparation, deployment, and post-deployment model monitoring and management. This includes applying advanced statistical and machine learning methods, causal inference, and experimental design to ensure models not only predict outcomes but drive measurable impact through real-world interventions.

The position operates within a multidisciplinary environment that includes cloud engineers, product managers, AI/automation engineers, application developers, architects, and enterprise platform teams. The Senior Data Scientist owns technical execution across the model lifecycle while partnering closely with product managers who drive product strategy, prioritization, and stakeholder alignment. The position reports to the JCHI Co-Director, who provides functional leadership for data science and AI initiatives and works across JCHI and Information Services stakeholders to align priorities, capabilities, and delivery.

This is a senior technical role that requires the ability to independently lead complex data science projects, mentor junior team members, and contribute to the strategic direction of the data science program. The role involves close collaboration with clinical and operational stakeholders to identify high-impact use cases, translate clinical questions into data science problems, and deliver AI solutions that create sustained value across the health system. This includes working across diverse data modalities (e.g., structured EHR data, time-series, imaging, and unstructured text) and leveraging state-of-the-art approaches, including predictive, generative, and hybrid models.

What We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate brings deep experience across the full AI model lifecycle in healthcare or complex enterprise environments, with demonstrated ability to independently lead projects from data exploration through production deployment and ongoing monitoring. Experience with healthcare EHR data, particularly Epic, is essential, and candidates should be comfortable working with complex, multimodal clinical datasets to develop models that drive measurable improvements in patient care and health system operations at scale.

Experience developing AI models using traditional machine learning, large language models, and hybrid approaches is strongly desired, including familiarity with cloud-based data science platforms such as AWS and modern ML infrastructure. Candidates should be highly proficient in Python, R, SQL, and related tools, with strong expertise in model evaluation, benchmarking, and performance optimization, as well as applying rigorous methods to ensure robustness, generalizability, and real-world impact.

Successful candidates will also demonstrate strong familiarity with enterprise health system operations and technologies, including electronic health records, healthcare data integration, and cloud platforms, along with the regulatory and privacy considerations unique to healthcare AI. The role requires the ability to work effectively across clinical, operational, technical, and vendor stakeholders, and to contribute to data science strategy in environments where innovation, scientific rigor, and patient safety must coexist.

Minimum Qualifications

Nine (9) years of related experience, education/training, OR a Bachelor’s degree in related area plus five (5) years of related experience/training. Related experience includes data science, computational science, machine learning, AI model development, and work with healthcare EHR data (e.g., Epic).
Advanced knowledge of HPC / data science / CI.
Highly advanced skills, and demonstrated experience associated with one or more of the following: HPC hardware and software power and performance analysis and research, design, modification, implementation and deployment of HPC or data science or CI applications and tools of large-scale scope.
Demonstrated ability to regularly, effectively communicate with unit-level management.
Demonstrated ability to initiate research proposals and acquire funding.
Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization and to external research and education audiences.
In depth skills and experience in independently resolving complex computing / data / CI problems using introductory and / or intermediate principles.
Self-motivated and works independently and as part of a team.
Advanced experience working in a complex computing / data / CI environment encompassing all or some of the following: HPC, data science infrastructure and tools / software, and diverse domain science application base.
In depth ability to successfully work and / or lead multiple concurrent projects. Demonstrated research and technology project leadership and management skills.
In depth experience assessing a broad spectrum of technical and research needs and demands and establish priorities, delegate and / or lead development of solutions to meet such needs.
Demonstrated advanced experience in one or more of the following: optimizing, benchmarking, HPC performance and power modeling, analyzing hardware, software, and applications for HPC / data / CI.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Computer/Computational/Data Science or Domain Sciences with computational specialization preferred.
Strong data science discipline across the full AI model lifecycle (intake, data prep, model development, evaluation, deployment, monitoring). Demonstrated ability to lead complex data science research projects with multi-institutional scope and serve as technical lead.
Healthcare data science platform experience in AWS, including model training, deployment, and monitoring.
Advanced proficiency in Python, R, SQL, ML frameworks, data visualization, and big-data/cloud platforms (AWS or Azure).
Experience developing AI models using traditional ML, LLMs, and hybrid approaches (generative and predictive AI applied to clinical/operational workflows).
In-depth experience with benchmarking, profiling, and performance analysis of data science code.
Experience with Epic EHR data and integrating AI solutions with Epic and related clinical data environments.
Operational familiarity with population health, clinical operations, or care coordination.
Experience evaluating and integrating vendor-based AI/data science platforms.
Experience operating within large academic medical centers or integrated delivery systems.
Demonstrated ability to translate model outputs into actionable clinical or operational interventions, and to support rigorous evaluation through real-world evidence generation, including opportunities for publication and multi-institutional collaboration
Ability to translate state-of-the-art methods into production-ready solutions within complex, real-world environments
Experience with causal inference, experimental design, or decision-focused modeling to evaluate and drive real-world interventions
Experience with prospective validation or study design in clinical or operational environments, including real-world evidence generation
Experience partnering across data engineering, clinical, operational, and executive stakeholders to define, develop, and sustain data science products in complex healthcare organizations
Operational familiarity with healthcare domains such as population health, clinical operations, or care coordination

SPECIAL CONDITIONS

jobs.title: Senior Scientist, Machine Learning and Algorithm Development for RNA Design
jobs.description:
The Role

Moderna is seeking a computational scientist to develop artificial intelligence, machine-learning, deep-learning, and optimization methods for therapeutic mRNA design.

This is a hands-on research role centered on translating biological questions into computational problems, developing and rigorously evaluating new algorithms, and turning those methods into reusable scientific software. The successful candidate will develop predictive and generative models that connect mRNA sequence and structure with experimentally measured properties.

The ideal candidate combines depth in AI/ML and algorithm development with the ability to reason about biological sequence and structure. Direct RNA or mRNA experience is highly valued, but we also welcome strong computational method developers from adjacent areas of biology who can demonstrate how their expertise transfers to RNA design.

Here’s What You’ll Do

Formulate mRNA design challenges as well-defined machine-learning and optimization problems, including appropriate objectives, constraints, datasets, and evaluation strategies.
Develop and benchmark predictive, generative, and optimization methods for biological sequence and structure.
Integrate mRNA sequence, predicted or experimentally measured structure, and high-throughput assay data into computational models.
Work closely with RNA biologists and experimental teams to design informative experiments, interpret results, and iteratively improve models.
Evaluate new approaches against meaningful baselines and determine where additional methodological complexity is—or is not—justified.
Build maintainable research software with clear documentation, testing, version control, and reproducible workflows.
Scale computational methods to large datasets using cloud or high-performance computing environments.
Communicate findings, limitations, and recommendations clearly to scientific and technical collaborators.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Basic Qualifications)

PhD in computer science, machine learning, computational biology, bioinformatics, statistics, bioengineering, physics, or a related quantitative field with 2+ years of experience.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing machine-learning, optimization, probabilistic, or other computational methods for biological or molecular data.
Strong Python programming skills and experience with modern scientific-computing or machine-learning frameworks.
Experience working with biological sequence, structure, or another form of molecular data.
Evidence of rigorous model evaluation, including appropriate baselines, validation strategies, and interpretation of model limitations.
Ability to translate an open-ended scientific question into a tractable computational research plan.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications)

Experience with RNA or mRNA biology, design, engineering, or therapeutics.
Experience with generative models, transformers, graph neural networks, representation learning, active learning, Bayesian optimization, or multi-objective optimization.
Familiarity with RNA secondary structure, ensemble properties, or chemical-probing data such as SHAPE.
Experience integrating high-throughput experimental or NGS-derived measurements with computational models.
Experience developing reusable scientific software rather than one-off analysis scripts.
Experience with cloud or distributed computing environments.
Publications, patents, or open-source work demonstrating a substantive contribution to algorithm or method development.
Ability to work effectively across computational and experimental teams.

Our Working Model

As we build our company, we have always believed that an in-person culture is critical to our success. This role is 100% onsite, reflecting the importance of being physically present to support the work, collaborate closely with colleagues, and contribute to our site-based operations.

Working onsite enables real-time collaboration, strong team connections, direct mentorship, and the hands-on partnership needed to deliver our mission. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.

Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.

Pay & Benefits

At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work.
That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.

Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs
A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support
Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support
Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown
Savings and investments to help you plan for the future
Location-specific perks and extras

The salary range for this role is $145,900.00 - $234,200.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance.

About Moderna

Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world.

By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities.

We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S.

If you want to make a difference and join a team that is changing the future of medicine, we invite you to visit modernatx.com/careers to learn more about our current opportunities.

Moderna is a place where everyone can grow. If you meet the Basic Qualifications for the role and you would be excited to contribute to our mission every day, please apply!

jobs.title: AI Software Engineer, Applications and Agents
jobs.description:
Basic Qualifications

Education Requirements:

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, or related Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics field, plus a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience; or Master's degree, plus 6 years relevant experience.

Due to the nature of work performed within our facilities, U.S. citizenship is required.

Responsibilities For This Position

ROLE AND POSITION OBJECTIVES:

The AI Software Engineer, Applications and Agents will design, code, test, evaluate, secure, deploy, and improve full-stack AI products. The engineer will work directly with users, domain experts, product owners, and technical teams to move from problem definition to working product and measurable outcome.

The role combines software engineering, enterprise data, and AI to build secure applications and re-engineer operations. The engineer will use approved cloud services, models, APIs, data, identity, security, and scalable application patterns across Azure and AWS. This is a hands-on individual-contributor software-engineering position.

What You Will Do

Build Production AI Applications and Agents

Design, write, test, integrate, review, deploy, and operate production AI applications, agents, APIs, services, and user experiences .
Work directly with business and engineering teams to build production-scale AI applications, agents, integrations, and end-to-end enterprise workflows .
Build agentic workflows using planning, reasoning, context management, retrieval, tool use, human approval, and multi-agent collaboration where appropriate.
Integrate approved commercial, open-weight, self-hosted, and GDMS-controlled models through secure interfaces and runtime services.
Develop full-stack products using modern frontend, backend, API, event-driven, data, and cloud-native engineering patterns.
Own delivery from ambiguous problem definition through architecture, implementation, testing, production release, adoption, support, and lifecycle improvement.
Build secure enterprise integrations with business systems, engineering tools, data services, identity, authorization, and workflow platforms.

Engineer AI Quality, Evaluation, and Safety

Define measurable product-quality, task-success, groundedness, safety, latency, reliability, and consumption criteria with product owners and AI Reliability Engineering.
Build automated evaluation pipelines, representative test suites, golden datasets, regression tests, integration tests, automated raters, and human-review workflows.
Evaluate prompts, instructions, context, retrieval, tools, model configurations, routing, and fallback behavior against approved use cases.
Implement controls for hallucination, prompt injection, data leakage, unsafe tool use, excessive autonomy, cross-tenant access, and policy violations.
Use red teaming, failure testing, observability, production feedback, and incident learning to improve application and agent behavior.

Deliver Secure and Supportable Products

Use approved CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, release, artifact, security, and evidence workflows to move products from source through supported production.
Build authentication, authorization, secrets, audit, data-protection, approval, stop, rollback, and recovery behavior into the product design.
Instrument metrics, logs, traces, quality signals, agent actions, model calls, tool use, latency, consumption, failure behavior, and user outcomes.
Serve as an engineering escalation point for complex application failures; troubleshoot across application, model, retrieval, tool, data, identity, network, and platform layers; and implement permanent corrections. Ongoing application support remains with the designated sustainment organization following transition.
Convert defects, incidents, and user feedback into regression tests, permanent engineering corrections, and reusable platform improvements.

Work Directly with Business and Mission Teams

Partner with functions, programs, engineers, and domain experts to decompose work, identify appropriate AI and non-AI solutions, and define measurable outcomes.
Re-engineer operational processes to reduce manual effort, improve flow and controls, and create scalable workflows that combine people, automation, and AI.
Develop prototypes only when needed to resolve uncertainty, then either productionize, transfer, or stop the work based on evidence.
Translate repeated product and workflow needs into reusable components, reference applications, templates, and integrations.
Measure adoption, task success, quality, cycle time, productivity, reliability, and mission or business impact after release.

Provide Senior Advanced Technical Direction

Work with limited instruction on complex, ambiguous, and undefined challenges that require original engineering judgment.
Define the scope, architecture, engineering evidence, schedule, risks, and acceptance expectations for work personally executed or technically led.
Provide code and architecture review, pairing, mentoring, and technical work direction without requiring people-management authority.
Use AI coding agents and engineering assistants for implementation, testing, review, diagnosis, documentation, and delivery while maintaining verification and accountability.
Keep current with commercial generative AI, agent, software-engineering, evaluation, cloud, security, and product-delivery practices; introduce validated improvements into GDMS engineering.

Required

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering or a related Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics field plus a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience; or a master's degree plus a minimum of 6 years of relevant experience.
Demonstrated advanced or expert proficiency coding, testing, integrating, documenting, deploying, and operating production software products.
Strong production coding ability in Python and at least one additional language such as TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++, C#, or Rust.
Experience delivering full-stack or backend cloud applications using APIs, data stores, eventing, authentication, authorization, testing, CI/CD, telemetry, and production support.
Hands-on experience building generative AI applications, agents, RAG solutions, tool-using workflows, or comparable intelligent systems in production.
Experience with prompt and context engineering, retrieval and grounding, memory, tool calling, orchestration, human-in-the-loop design, and agent evaluation.
Experience integrating enterprise data, APIs, business systems, identity, permissions, and secure tool execution into production applications.
Experience building automated tests and evaluations for functional behavior, model and agent quality, safety, reliability, latency, and regressions.
Production experience integrating enterprise data and cloud-native AI services across Azure and AWS, including model APIs, orchestration, storage, eventing, identity, security, telemetry, and modern containerized or serverless application patterns.
Demonstrated ability to solve ambiguous problems, work directly with technical and nontechnical users, and own delivery through production and measurable outcome.
Demonstrated written and verbal communication skills, including explaining architecture, model behavior, risk, tradeoffs, and product evidence to technical and executive audiences.

Workplace Options:

This position is hybrid near a major GDMS facility preferred. Remote may be considered for an exceptional candidate able to support periodic on-site collaboration with product and mission teams.

jobs.description:
Discover What’s Possible At BetMGM

Ready to make your career legendary? Join us as we bring the magic of Vegas to our players. The BetMGM team has over 1,400 talented members, revolutionizing sports betting and online gaming in the United States and Canada. We’re a brand with technology at our hearts and the most driven and focused talent in the business.

Benefits

As a valued team member, we’re committed to giving you the resources and support you need to thrive. Our benefits and perks include:

Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, and Disability Insurance
401(k) with company match
Pre-tax spending accounts including health care FSA and commuter savings
Flexible paid time off
Professional development reimbursement and ongoing skills training opportunities
Employee resource groups
Swag, ticket giveaways, and more!

At BetMGM, we recognize that every individual plays a meaningful role in our success. That’s why we’re committed to building a respectful, inclusive workplace. It’s the strategy behind every win. By meeting people where they are, we create a culture of belonging where everyone can thrive and a workplace that reflects our values, our people, and our drive to win.

The Opportunity

About The Role

The Sr. MLOps Engineer treats ML systems as software systems and owns the path from a trained model to a production endpoint that meets its latency, cost, and reliability budgets — across both batch scoring (SageMaker Batch Transform, Snowflake Cortex / Snowpark ML, dbt-orchestrated scoring) and real-time inference (SageMaker real-time endpoints, Lambda + Bedrock, sub-second feature serving). The Sr. Engineer builds the platform that data scientists and ML engineers ship on: feature store with guaranteed online/offline parity, model registry, CI/CD for ML, drift and quality monitoring, champion/challenger and shadow deployment scaffolding. This requires a software-engineering-first mindset — distributed systems, observability, and on-call instincts are the foundation; ML literacy makes them effective for this role. GenAI integration experience is a plus, not a requirement.

Responsibilities

ML Production Platform
Stand up and operate BetMGM's ML platform on AWS (SageMaker Training, Model Registry, Pipelines, Endpoints, Batch Transform) and Snowflake (Snowpark ML, Cortex), with Terraform-managed infrastructure
Build self-service scaffolds that let data scientists ship a model end-to-end without a ticket queue — cookie-cutter project templates with CI, drift monitoring, alerting, IaC, and Snowflake connectivity pre-baked

Batch and Real-Time Inference
Design and operate batch scoring pipelines — SageMaker Batch Transform, dbt-orchestrated scoring against Snowflake, Snowpark ML — with explicit freshness and cost SLAs.
Design and operate real-time inference paths — SageMaker real-time endpoints, Lambda + Bedrock for GenAI, API Gateway — with stated latency budgets (typically sub-100ms) and graceful degradation under load.
Own the feature store (SageMaker Feature Store, Tecton, or Feast) with guaranteed online/offline parity — training-serving skew is treated as an incident, not a tradeoff.

CI/CD and Deployment Patterns
Build CI/CD for ML — model registry, automated retraining triggers, model versioning, lineage from feature → training run → deployed model → live prediction.
Implement champion/challenger, shadow deployments, and canary releases as platform primitives so individual model teams do not reinvent them per project.

Monitoring, Drift & Reliability
Stand up drift detection, data quality, and model performance monitoring (Evidently, Arize, or SageMaker Model Monitor — pick one and standardize) with paging that routes to humans who can fix it.
Own MLOps incident response — production model failures are SEV events with postmortems.

Cost and Performance
Right-size endpoints, batch caching, request batching, and autoscaling. State cost-per-prediction targets up front and meet them.

GenAI Integration (Plus, Not Required)
Integrate LLM APIs (Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI) into production paths — RAG pipelines, agent eval frameworks, prompt versioning, cost and latency observability.
Partner with the Helix team on AI personalization workloads as they ramp toward March Madness 2027.
undefined
AI in the Engineering Loop
Direct AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, dbt Copilot) as a force multiplier across infrastructure code, eval suites, and model-serving glue — designing work for agents to do, not just accepting their suggestions.

Collaboration
Partner with the data engineering team on shared standards (Terraform modules, CI/CD patterns, observability, lineage).
Work alongside data scientists and analytics partners to land the right interfaces between research and production — opinionated about the boundary.
Coordinate with Entain India and contractor ML partners as workloads consolidate onto the BetMGM-owned platform.

Qualifications
BS or MS in Computer Science, Math, Statistics, Machine Learning, or other STEM field — or equivalent practical experience. Practical experience wins ties; a PhD is neither required nor a tiebreakers
Must-Haves

jobs.description:
Aimpoint Digital is a market-leading data, AI, analytics, and operations research advisory and solution engineering firm. We help organizations design, build, and operationalize enterprise-grade data and AI platforms, decision intelligence solutions, optimization systems, and production AI applications.

We are not a commodity consulting firm. We are a technical partner to organizations that need to move beyond experimentation and deploy AI into real business workflows with the architecture, governance, reliability, and engineering discipline required for production.

We believe successful AI initiatives require much more than prompting an LLM. They require strong software engineering, scalable architecture, reliable deployment, thoughtful evaluation, and disciplined engineering practices.

About The Role

As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer, you will work directly with clients to design, build, deploy, and scale enterprise AI solutions. You will combine strong software engineering fundamentals with modern AI technologies to deliver production-ready systems that create measurable business value.

You will work across the entire AI engineering lifecycle; from solution architecture and application development to deployment, evaluation, and operationalization.

What You Will Do

Design, build, and deploy production AI applications, copilots, retrieval systems, and agentic workflows
Translate business problems into scalable technical solutions using modern AI engineering best practices
Develop backend services, APIs, and application architectures that integrate AI capabilities into enterprise systems
Build multi-agent systems, AI agents, workflow automation, and decision-support systems
Deploy AI solutions into production with appropriate security, observability, monitoring, evaluation, and governance
Design AI systems that integrate with enterprise data platforms, APIs, databases, messaging systems, and business applications
Collaborate with cross-functional client teams including engineering, data, product, architecture, security, and business stakeholders

Contribute reusable accelerators, frameworks, technical assets, and thought leadership that strengthen the AI Engineering practice
Stay current with emerging AI technologies and recommend practical approaches that improve client outcomes

We are looking for engineers who enjoy solving difficult technical problems and building production software. You are comfortable moving between software engineering, AI application development, cloud architecture, and client collaboration.

You understand that successful AI systems require excellent engineering, not just excellent models.

3+ years of professional software engineering experience building production applications
1+ years designing and deploying AI or machine learning solutions into production

Experience with MLOps, LLMOps, or production deployment pipelines

Experience integrating AI applications with enterprise data sources, APIs, and business systems
Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, GCP, Databricks, Snowflake, or similar technologies
Experience deploying applications using containers, Kubernetes, serverless platforms, or similar cloud-native technologies
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Ability to independently own technical workstreams while collaborating across multidisciplinary teams

Preferred Qualifications

One or more of the following is a plus:

Experience developing production APIs using frameworks such as FastAPI, Flask, Spring Boot, .NET, and Express
Experience building multi-agent systems, AI automated workflows, agents, semantic search, vector databases, or knowledge graph retrieval applications

Experience deploying AI solutions serving 1000+ users
Consulting experience or experience working directly with enterprise customers

jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.description:
Leads and executes deep dive diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics to support data-driven business decision making. Mentors and develops junior data scientists and analysts.

Vanguard is committed to continuous Client Experience improvement, and the Enterprise Intelligence group develops and supports a suite of internal CX analytical tools. These Data Science tools – spanning models, software, and interfaces – are used by internal Vanguard expert analysts to better understand CX outcomes. This position is for a full stack Data Scientist supporting the continued development of our internal suite of CX analytical tools. The role will be responsible for rapidly understanding the current state of those methods / models / systems, then working with existing Data Science and Machine Learning stakeholders to support and update that suite.

Applicants should have a baseline understanding of the Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC), deployment of code through Python packages, integration of AI into code (both in development and application), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) fundamentals for text processing & analysis. Your work will connect with subject matter experts across Data Science, Analytics, Client Experience, and Business – you’ll need to be able to cater your technical communication across audiences. You will follow the Vanguard Model Governance process and adhere to AI usage policies, protecting client information and ensuring full compliance with safety & security best practices.

You’ll be working with a highly-skilled team of Data Scientists and Machine Learning Engineers, on a suite of software that has moved beyond its initial development stages. This will demand rapid familiarization, the ability to quickly understand existing codebase, and finding opportunities for improvement. You will need to work with your management and stakeholders to prioritize tasking, autonomously deliver on that tasking, and proactively come back with proposed next steps.

Core Responsibilities

Deliver technology:

Build and support existing software, models, packages, and other analytics tools used for data-driven business decision making.
Implement AI prompt engineering, NLP text processing, and unstructured data modeling in systems & packages.
Deploy software to internal consumers, adhere to the PDLC process, create and use monitoring & tracking features.

Use technology responsibly:

Follow the Vanguard Model Governance methodology & process, adhering to security policies around AI usage, software design, and model validation.
Identify and diagnose data & code issues, always through continuous code review, and when necessary by performing root-cause analysis and post-mortems.
Proactively surface found issues or risks.

Manage stakeholders:

Engage with internal stakeholders (DS, MLE, Business...) to understand and probe business processes in order to improve CX models, packages, and tools.
Establish Definitions-of-Done with stakeholders, ensure that DoD is tracked and met through the PDLC process.
Communicate complex findings and implications to leaders & teammates.

Be a team player:

Mentor and develop junior data scientists and analysts.
Actively share information across workstreams, promote cross-pollination of findings & hurdles.
Participate in special projects and perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum of five years related work experience in Data Science development & modeling roles.
Undergraduate degree in Computer Science or related Data Science field of study, or equivalent combination of training and experience. Graduate degree preferred.
Experience with the Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC), especially deploying Data Science tools to expert analyst users.
Proven experience using AI and NLP methods & tools to extract information from unstructured data at scale. Strong background using quantified measures to evaluate text, developing models around those measures, and improving them over time.
Advanced programming experience with Python, including deploying solutions as Packages that include telemetry feedback, safeguards, secure credentialing, and other User Access Controls (UAC).
Ability to communicate technically complex concepts across varying audiences. Know when to dive deep, and when to keep things high-level.
Some experience with data wrangling required – ability to extract, transform and load (ETL) large-scale data for statistical modeling.
Preference for candidates who have worked with Client Experience & client outcomes, who have familiarity with terminology surrounding client feedback & stories.

Special Factors

Sponsorship

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

About Vanguard

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

How We Work

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/04/2026.

Bachelor's degree required
5+ years of applicable experience
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Software Engineering: Strong proficiency in Python and Git, grounded in core software engineering practice including modular design, API design, testing, code review, and CI/CD.
Cloud Solution Architecture: Experience designing and deploying solutions on Azure, GCP, or AWS, including the security, integration, and cost considerations that shape design.
Design Trade-offs and Technical Judgment: Ability to translate business objectives into technical options, and to explain the effort, risk, and value of each in terms stakeholders can act on, driving decisions on scope, sequencing, and architecture.

jobs.title: Founding ML Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
About Parisi Labs

Parisi Labs is building foundational world models for physical industry. We are developing models that learn how complex physical systems behave and reuse that understanding across forecasts, scenarios, and operational decisions.

Energy is our first proving ground. We combine historical and live data with operational context, bringing together machine learning research, data infrastructure, and software engineering to turn advances in modeling into useful technology for energy operators.

We are a small technical team working directly with the founders on our core models, systems, and products.

About The Role

We are looking for a Founding ML Platform Engineer to design, build, and own the infrastructure that takes our machine learning models from research into reliable production systems.

You will establish the core MLOps platform at Parisi Labs, creating the tools and workflows that allow researchers to operationalize models without becoming responsible for the infrastructure around them. This includes model registries, dataset and experiment lineage, retraining workflows, scheduled batch inference, and production monitoring.

Our models operate on complex, time-dependent data, producing forecasts and simulations of physical systems. You will build the infrastructure that makes these workflows reproducible, observable, and dependable as our research and products evolve.

This is a hands-on founding engineering role with significant technical ownership. You will work directly with our CTO, Chief Scientist, and researchers to define the platform architecture, select technologies, and implement the systems the company will build on.

What You'll Own

Design and build our end-to-end MLOps platform, from model registration and versioning through deployment, inference, and monitoring.
Develop reliable, scalable batch inference infrastructure for recurring forecasts and model-generated simulations.
Build model registries and lineage systems that track training inputs, dataset versions, model configurations, artifacts, and deployment history.
Create standardized workflows and tools that allow researchers to register models, manage experiments, and move models into production.
Develop automated retraining and deployment pipelines, including dataset preparation, validation, version promotion, and rollback.
Build monitoring and observability for model performance, forecast accuracy, data drift, pipeline health, and production failures.
Help steer the technical and research direction of the company.

What we're looking for

6+ years of software engineering experience, including significant hands-on experience building and operating production ML systems.
A track record of designing and owning ML infrastructure or MLOps platforms, ideally having built systems from the ground up.
Strong Python and backend engineering skills, with experience building reliable data processing and distributed workflow systems.
Experience with ML lifecycle tooling such as MLflow, orchestration frameworks such as Dagster, Airflow, or Prefect, and modern cloud infrastructure.
Deep familiarity with model deployment, batch inference, model versioning, data lineage, and production monitoring.
Comfort working closely with ML researchers and translating experimental workflows into reliable engineering systems.
An entrepreneurial mindset, strong technical ownership, and the ability to operate independently in a fast-moving environment with limited structure.

Especially compelling backgrounds:

Experience as a founder, technical co-founder, or founding engineer at an early-stage startup.
Experience building an ML platform from zero to production, rather than exclusively maintaining established infrastructure.
Experience as an early technical hire who helped establish engineering architecture, tooling, and practices.
Experience with time-series forecasting, energy systems, or other data-intensive scientific applications.

First 90 days

30 days: Understand our research workflows, existing model infrastructure, and production forecasting systems. Identify the most important gaps in model lifecycle management, serving, and observability.
60 days: Establish foundational model registry and lineage capabilities, and deliver an initial standardized workflow for moving research models into production.
90 days: Own a reliable end-to-end production ML workflow, including model versioning, scheduled inference, monitoring, and clear operational visibility.

Why join

You will establish the platform that all of our models run on. Your work will determine how our research becomes reliable, scalable technology used to support real-world decisions.

As an early engineering hire, you will have substantial ownership over our infrastructure, architecture, and engineering practices, working directly with the founders and researchers developing our core technology.

Location and compensation

Location:
New York City. This is an in-person role.

Salary range:
$200,000–$280,000 USD.

Equity
: meaningful early-company equity.
